content: Administer an 8-gram suppository as needed for constipation. The patient should retain the suppository for 15 minutes. Before insertion, remove the protective wrapper. Gently insert the tip of the suppository into the rectum using a slight side-to-side motion, ensuring the tip is pointed toward the navel. For liquid suppositories, squeeze the bulb until all the liquid is expelled, then discard the unit. Potential side effects include excessive bowel activity, cramping pain, rectal irritation, and tenesmus. This product is intended for rectal use only and may cause rectal discomfort, including a burning sensation. Do not use this product if the patient experiences abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or a sudden change in bowel habits lasting more than two weeks. Additionally, avoid use if the patient has already used a laxative for more than one week unless directed by a physician. Frequent or prolonged use of laxatives may lead to dependency. Discontinue use and seek medical attention if rectal bleeding occurs or if there is no bowel movement after using the product, as these symptoms may require physician care. Do not use this product for longer than one week. Regarding pregnancy, there is no available data on the safety of this product. For lactating individuals, it is not known whether the product is excreted in breast milk, but no risks to nursing infants have been identified. In general, this product is considered acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
